messages:
ash: quick update — I ran the dynamic pad-threshold probe on the 4xA100 flame nodes this morning. numbers look...interesting.

maria: interesting how?

ash: batch growth stayed stable but padding waste dropped ~12% on average for short seqs (<=128). big wins when kv-hit-rate > 0.6.

ryan: sweet. did kernel selection change?

ash: yes, we routed short seqs to the fast-vec kernel when effective_seq_len < pad_threshold. kernel switch cost ~0.7ms on cold kernels but amortized out for 50+ token batches.

maria: can you paste the snippet of the experiment config?

ash: sure:

```
pad_threshold: 96
pad_policy: dynamic
workspace_headroom: 0.12
kernel_policy: fast-vec-if-short
kv_cache_probe_window: 300s
```

ryan: did you change workspace sizing? sounds like headroom is small.

ash: reduced workspace_headroom from 0.2 -> 0.12. memory tail is tighter but reclaim path handled transient spikes. saw 3 reclaim-triggered kernel fallbacks, no OOMs.

sara: what about per-seq overhead? we worry about per-request allocations causing fragmentation.

ash: profiled allocator: per-seq meta ~1.2KB allocated, reclaimed via slab freelist. fragmentation index improved by 4 points. but padding reduction shifted some pressure into kv cache because effective keyset bigger.

maria: so tradeoff: less pad waste but more KV working set. any perf regressions on p99 latency?

ash: small reg at p99 for bursts with many long seqs — about +3ms. can mitigate by short-circuiting kernel switch when batch has >30% long sequences. put a guard in batching heuristic.

ryan: logs/snippet from perf-bot?

perf-bot: experiment 1998123456: pad_waste_delta=-12.1%, frac_kv_evictions=+4.8%, p50 latency=-1.3ms, p95 latency=-0.9ms, p99 latency=+3.2ms, ooms=0.

ash: i'll push a small heuristic tweak: if batch.long_seq_fraction > 0.3 then prefer uniform pad to avoid kernel thrash. submitting PR now.

maria: also let's add a KV-aware pad threshold: raise pad_threshold by 32 when kv_eviction_rate > 5% in last 5m. may stabilize working set.

ryan: good idea. add a safe rollback window and perf regression alert in the rollout.

ash: noted. I'll roll canary to 10% traffic, 15m check. oncall-bot will page if p99 > baseline + 10ms.

oncall-bot: will page on threshold breach.

sara: quick note for the writeup: include a short table of seq buckets, pad waste per-bucket, kv-eviction delta. helps PMs reason about tradeoffs.

ash: will do. TL;DR: dynamic pad threshold + smaller headroom -> meaningful token-cost savings for short-heavy workloads, slight p99 regressions on mixed long bursts; mitigation via batch heuristic + kv-aware thresholds.

maria: thanks — super actionable. :thumbsup:
